s: What was the primary business activity of the English settlements in Andhra Pradesh during the early colonial period, particularly at Fort St. George?
Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam areas are famous for their produce?
x:
Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam, located along the coastal belt of present-day Prakasam district, have been famous since ancient times for salt production. The favourable coastal climate, extensive salt pans and proximity to the sea enabled large- scale manufacture of salt. During the medieval and colonial periods, salt produced in these regions was transported to different parts of Andhra and neighbouring areas. Salt production became an important source of livelihood for local communities and contributed significantly to the regional economy.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: In which district did the manganese industry maintain the first position in the world between 1892–1929 in manganese production?
x:
Between 1892 and 1929, the Nellore district gained international recognition for its rich manganese deposits and occupied a leading position in world manganese production. The manganese mined from Nellore was exported to several countries and was widely used in the iron and steel industry. The mining sector contributed significantly to the economic development of the region during the colonial period.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
